# Load libraries and data

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Preserve Unicode symbols in plot text on Windows.
if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", ".UTF-8")
.libPaths(c(".r_library", .libPaths()))
library(scico)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(sf)
# Default image dimensions in inches and raster resolution.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5, dpi = 300, fig.retina = 1,
                      fig.align = "center", dev = "ragg_png")

# Keep a separate high-resolution PNG for every figure produced while knitting.
plot_export_dir = file.path(getwd(), "plots_png", "nature")
dir.create(plot_export_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
plot_filename = function(path) {
  name = sub("-[0-9]+[.]png$", "", basename(path))
  if (name == "ai-waffles") {
    index = as.integer(sub(".*-([0-9]+)[.]png$", "\\1", basename(path)))
    name = paste0("ai-waffle-", ai_questions[index])
  }
  name = gsub("-", "_", name)
  if (!endsWith(name, "_nature")) name = paste0(name, "_nature")
  paste0(name, ".png")
}

default_plot_hook = knitr::knit_hooks$get("plot")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {
  for (path in x) {
    filename = plot_filename(path)
    file.copy(path, file.path(plot_export_dir, filename), overwrite = TRUE)
  }
  default_plot_hook(x, options)
})
```

# Question titles


```{r question-titles}
question_text = c(
  discipline_of_interest = "Select your primary research discipline.",
  stage = "Select your career stage.",
  ai_use = "How much do you currently use AI?",
  awareness = "Before reading the introduction above, how familiar were you with the recent reports of AI-generated mathematics research?",
  capability = "Within the next three years, what level of scientific research capability do you expect AI systems to achieve in your field?",
  displacement = "Advances in AI will significantly reduce the demand for human researchers in my field in the next three years.",
  threat = "Advances in AI threaten the continued existence and long-term viability of academic research as a human profession.",
  opportunity = "AI-driven research will increase the overall rate of scientific progress.",
  concern = "I am concerned about the implications of AI-driven scientific research for my own job security.",
  ai_roles = "Highest level of AI autonomy you consider acceptable by research roles",
  change = "Have recent advances in AI-driven scientific research caused you to reconsider your research or academic career?",
  country = ""
)

question_title = function(question, width = 85) {
  stringr::str_wrap(unname(question_text[question]), width = width)
}

title_height = function(title) {
  0.27 * (stringr::str_count(title, "\n") + 1)
}

```

```{r response-order}
    "Perform research tasks independently, but produce lower-quality results than competent human researchers.",
    "Perform research tasks independently, producing results of comparable quality to those of competent human researchers.",
```

# Plot appearance and layout

```{r plot-helpers}
plot_base_size = 14
plot_label_size = 12
plot_font = "serif"

stacked_percent_label = function(proportion) {
  percentage = round(100 * proportion)
  ifelse(!is.na(percentage) & percentage >= 5, paste0(percentage, "%"), "")
}

participant_subtitle = function(n) {
  paste0("<i>N</i> = ", format(n, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))
}

notes = function(text) {
  paste0("<i>Note.</i> ", gsub("\n", " ", text, fixed = TRUE))
}

# Five colours shared by all plots; separate bars use one colour.
tokyo_colours = scico::scico(5, palette = "vik")
academic_colours = list(
  responses = tokyo_colours,
  bar = tokyo_colours[2], low = tokyo_colours[5], high = tokyo_colours[1],
  missing = "#DDDDDD"
)
response_palette = function(answers) {
  positions = if (length(answers) == 4) c(1, 2, 4, 5) else seq_along(answers)
  setNames(academic_colours$responses[positions], answers)
}

# Explicit line breaks keep the long legend options compact and predictable.
legend_response_labels = function(question, answers, percentages = NULL) {
  labels = if (question == "capability") {
    c("Cannot help", "Assist humans",
      "Work independently:\nachieving lower quality",
      "Work independently:\nachieving comparable quality",
      "Work independently:\nachieving higher quality")
  } else {
    wrapped = stringr::str_wrap(answers, width = 22)
    wrapped[answers == "Neither agree nor disagree"] = "Neither agree nor disagree"
    wrapped
  }
  if (!is.null(percentages)) {
    percentage_labels = paste0(" (", scales::percent(percentages, accuracy = 0.1), ")")
    labels = vapply(seq_along(labels), function(i) {
      if (question == "capability") {
        if (grepl("\n", labels[i], fixed = TRUE)) {
          sub("\n", paste0(percentage_labels[i], "\n"), labels[i], fixed = TRUE)
        } else {
          paste0(labels[i], "\n", trimws(percentage_labels[i]))
        }
      } else if (answers[i] == "Neither agree nor disagree") {
        paste0(labels[i], percentage_labels[i])
      } else {
        paste0(labels[i], "\n", trimws(percentage_labels[i]))
      }
    }, character(1))
  }
  labels
}

# Keep colour swatches square even when a legend label spans several lines.
draw_key_square = function(data, params, size) {
  grid::rectGrob(width = grid::unit(12, "pt"), height = grid::unit(12, "pt"),
                 gp = grid::gpar(fill = data$fill, col = NA))
}

theme_nature = function(base_size = plot_base_size) {
  ink = "#222222"
  background = "white"

  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = plot_font) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = ink),
      geom = element_geom(family = plot_font, fontsize = plot_label_size),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = background, color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = background, color = NA),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_size + 4, face = "bold",
                                margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(size = base_size, color = "#596675",
                                   margin = margin(b = 12)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = base_size),
      axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
      axis.text = element_text(size = plot_label_size, color = ink),
      axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1, lineheight = 1.05,
                                 margin = margin(r = 10)),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = ink, linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks.length = grid::unit(3, "pt"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.location = "plot",
      legend.justification = "center",
      legend.box.just = "center",
      legend.direction = "horizontal",
      legend.box.spacing = grid::unit(2, "pt"),
      legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 2),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(12, "pt"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = base_size),
      legend.text = element_text(size = base_size),
      strip.text = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      plot.caption = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        size = plot_label_size, family = plot_font, hjust = 0, vjust = 0,
        width = grid::unit(1, "npc"), lineheight = 1.1, margin = margin(t = 14)),
      plot.margin = margin(16, 24, 16, 16)
    )
}

category_plot = function(counts, title,
                         wrap_width = 32,
                         response_order = NULL, denominator = NULL, participants = NULL) {
  counts = counts |>
    mutate(response = as.character(response)) |>
    filter(!is.na(response), nzchar(trimws(response)))
  if (nrow(counts) == 0) return(NULL)
  if (is.null(participants)) participants = sum(counts$n)

  # Never sort by count. Reverse levels because ggplot draws the first at bottom.
  if (is.null(response_order)) response_order = sort(unique(counts$response))
  unknown = setdiff(counts$response, response_order)
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("Add these responses to response_orders: ", paste(unknown, collapse = "; "))
  }
  if (is.null(denominator)) {
    denominator = if ("denominator" %in% names(counts))
      setNames(counts$denominator, counts$response) else sum(counts$n)
  }
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(denominator)), all(denominator > 0))
  if (length(denominator) > 1) stopifnot(all(response_order %in% names(denominator)))
  counts = counts |>
    tidyr::complete(response = response_order, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
    mutate(value = n / if (length(.env$denominator) == 1) .env$denominator else
             unname(.env$denominator[response]),
           label = scales::percent(value, accuracy = 1),
           response = factor(response, levels = rev(response_order)))
  wrapped = stringr::str_wrap(levels(counts$response), width = wrap_width)
  # Reserve at least 0.42 inches per row, plus space for multiline labels.
  height = 1.8 + sum(pmax(0.42, 0.19 * (stringr::str_count(wrapped, "\n") + 1) + 0.16))

  p = ggplot(counts, aes(x = value, y = response)) +
    geom_col(fill = academic_colours$bar, width = 0.68) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.2,
              color = "#222222") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = wrap_width)) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
      breaks = function(x) {
        ticks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)(x)
        ticks[ticks >= 0 & ticks <= 1]
      },
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
    ) +
    labs(title = stringr::str_wrap(title, width = 62),
         subtitle = participant_subtitle(participants),
         x = "Share of respondents",
         y = NULL) +
    theme_nature()
  attr(p, "figure_height") = max(4, height) + 0.4 + title_height(stringr::str_wrap(title, 62))
  p
}

# Group comparisons: one complete response distribution per group.
grouped_ai_plot = function(data, question, group, group_order, group_title,
                            rank_responses = NULL, hierarchy_parent = NULL) {
  answers = response_orders[[question]]
  if (is.null(answers)) stop("Missing response order for ", question)
  plot_data = data |>
    transmute(group = as.character(.data[[group]]),
              response = as.character(.data[[question]])) |>
    filter(!is.na(group), nzchar(trimws(group)),
           !is.na(response), nzchar(trimws(response)))
  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) return(NULL)
  stopifnot(all(plot_data$response %in% answers),
            all(plot_data$group %in% group_order))
  all_responses = as.character(data[[question]])
  all_responses = all_responses[!is.na(all_responses) & nzchar(trimws(all_responses))]
  stopifnot(all(all_responses %in% answers))
  # Pool the parent from original respondents, including missing subfields.
  # Keep all_responses unchanged so the overall bar never double-counts people.
  child_groups = character()
  if (!is.null(hierarchy_parent)) {
    child_groups = unique(as.character(data[[group]][data$discipline_1 %in% hierarchy_parent]))
    child_groups = intersect(group_order, setdiff(child_groups, hierarchy_parent))
    parent_data = data |>
      filter(discipline_1 == hierarchy_parent) |>
      transmute(group = hierarchy_parent, response = as.character(.data[[question]])) |>
      filter(!is.na(response), nzchar(trimws(response)))
    plot_data = bind_rows(plot_data, parent_data)
    group_order = unique(c(group_order, hierarchy_parent))
  }
  groups = group_order[group_order %in% plot_data$group]
  is_agreement = identical(answers, agreement_order)
  # Agreement questions rank by strong agreement, then somewhat agreement.
  # Calculate shares among valid answers, retaining the supplied order for ties.
  if (is_agreement) {
    ranking = plot_data |>
      group_by(group) |>
      summarise(strong_agree_share = mean(response == "Strongly agree"),
                somewhat_agree_share = mean(response == "Somewhat agree"), .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(tie_order = match(group, groups)) |>
      arrange(desc(strong_agree_share),
              if (is.null(hierarchy_parent)) desc(somewhat_agree_share) else tie_order,
              tie_order)
    groups = ranking$group
  } else if (!is.null(rank_responses)) {
    stopifnot(all(rank_responses %in% answers))
    ranking = plot_data |>
      group_by(group) |>
      summarise(rank_share = mean(response %in% rank_responses), .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(tie_order = match(group, groups)) |>
      arrange(desc(rank_share), tie_order)
    groups = ranking$group
  }

  if (!is.null(hierarchy_parent) && hierarchy_parent %in% groups) {
    children = groups[groups %in% child_groups]
    parents = groups[!groups %in% child_groups]
    groups = append(parents, children, after = match(hierarchy_parent, parents))
  }
  groups = c("All respondents", groups)
  segments = bind_rows(plot_data, tibble(group = "All respondents", response = all_responses)) |>
    count(group, response) |>
    complete(group = groups, response = answers, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
    mutate(response = factor(response, levels = answers)) |>
    arrange(group, response) |>
    group_by(group) |>
    mutate(total = sum(n), proportion = n / total,
           xmax = cumsum(proportion),
           xmin = xmax - proportion) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(y = match(group, rev(groups)) + if_else(group == "All respondents", 0.5, 0),
           label = stacked_percent_label(proportion))
  stopifnot(all(abs(tapply(segments$proportion, segments$group, sum) - 1) < 1e-10),
            all(segments$xmax >= segments$xmin))

  palette = response_palette(answers)
  # Choose black or white text by the larger luminance contrast.
  rgb = grDevices::col2rgb(palette) / 255
  linear_rgb = ifelse(rgb <= 0.04045, rgb / 12.92, ((rgb + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  luminance = colSums(linear_rgb * c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722))
  text_colors = ifelse((1.05 / (luminance + 0.05)) > ((luminance + 0.05) / 0.05),
                       "white", "black")
  segments$text_color = text_colors[as.integer(segments$response)]
  legend_labels = legend_response_labels(question, answers)
  axis_labels = stringr::str_wrap(rev(groups), 31)
  if (!is.null(hierarchy_parent)) {
    child_rows = rev(groups) %in% child_groups
    axis_labels[child_rows] = paste0("    ", gsub("\n", "\n    ", axis_labels[child_rows], fixed = TRUE))
  }
  title = question_title(question, width = 90)
  caption = "Labels shown for segments with percentages ≥ 5%."
  caption = paste0(caption, " Percentages exclude missing answers to this question.",
                    " All respondents are shown separately and pools valid answers from the full filtered sample.")
  if (group == "country_group") {
    countries = data |>
      filter(!is.na(.data[[group]]), nzchar(trimws(.data[[group]])),
             !is.na(.data[[question]]), nzchar(trimws(.data[[question]]))) |>
      summarise(n = n_distinct(country_iso3, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
      pull(n)
    caption = paste0(caption, " Countries represented: ", countries, ".")
  }
  if (is_agreement && is.null(hierarchy_parent)) {
    caption = paste0(caption, " Items are ordered by the percentage selecting Strongly agree, with ties broken by the percentage selecting Somewhat agree.")
  }

  if (!is.null(hierarchy_parent)) {
    caption = paste0(caption, " ", hierarchy_parent,
      " pools all valid answers in that discipline, including unspecified subfields.",
      if (is_agreement) " Disciplines are ranked by Strongly agree; indented natural-science fields are ranked by Strongly agree only within their parent segment. Ties retain the original discipline order." else
        " Indented natural-science fields are ranked only within their parent segment.")
  }
  caption = paste0(caption, " Percentages may not total 100 because of rounding.")

  p = ggplot(segments) +
    geom_rect(key_glyph = draw_key_square, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.40,
                  ymax = y + 0.40, fill = response), color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = y, label = label, color = text_color),
              show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(palette, answers), breaks = answers,
                      labels = legend_labels, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(segments$y)), labels = axis_labels,
                       limits = c(0.35, length(groups) + 1.25),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1), oob = scales::oob_keep,
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = participant_subtitle(length(all_responses)),
         x = "Share of respondents within each group",
         y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = notes(caption)) +
    theme_nature() +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8), lineheight = 1.1),
          plot.margin = margin(16, 65, 16, 16),
          plot.title = element_text(margin = margin(b = 12)),
          plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(margin = margin(b = 6), lineheight = 1.15),
          legend.text = element_text(lineheight = 1.05))
  if (!is.null(hierarchy_parent)) {
    p = p + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0))
    attr(p, "indented_groups") = child_groups
  }
  # Equal row spacing must accommodate the longest wrapped group label.
  row_height = max(0.85, max(stringr::str_count(axis_labels, "\n") + 1) * 0.20 + 0.22)
  # Reserve title/legend space separately so even two-group charts have thick bars.
  attr(p, "figure_height") = max(6, 3.9 + (length(groups) + 0.5) * row_height + title_height(title) + if (is_agreement) 0.6 else 0)
  attr(p, "figure_width") = 12
  attr(p, "figure_label") = paste("grouped", group, question, sep = "-")
  p
}

grouped_plots = list()

# Child chunks give every plot in a loop its own device height when knitting.
show_survey_plot = function(p, name = NULL) {
  if (is.null(p)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (!isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) {
    print(p)
    return(invisible(p))
  }
  height = attr(p, "figure_height")
  width = attr(p, "figure_width")
  if (is.null(width)) width = 12
  label = if (is.null(name)) attr(p, "figure_label") else name
  if (is.null(label)) label = ""
  output = knitr::knit_child(
    text = sprintf("```{r %s, echo=FALSE, fig.width=%.2f, fig.height=%.2f}\nprint(p)\n```",
                   label, width, height),
    envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE
  )
  cat(output, sep = "\n")
}
```

# Participant summary

Counts use the filtered sample. Percentages exclude missing or blank answers
within each variable and are rounded to one decimal place.

```{r participant-summary}
summary_rows = function(variable, heading, responses, labels = responses) {
  answers = trimws(as.character(data_filtered[[variable]]))
  answers = answers[!is.na(answers) & nzchar(answers)]
  counts = as.integer(table(factor(answers, levels = responses)))
  data.frame(
    Variable = c(heading, labels),
    Count = c(NA_integer_, counts),
    `Percentage (%)` = c(NA_real_, round(100 * counts / length(answers), 1)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

summary_disciplines = c(
  "Natural sciences", "Engineering and technology",
  "Medical, health and life sciences", "Agricultural and veterinary sciences",
  "Social sciences", "Humanities and the arts"
)
participant_summary = rbind(
  summary_rows("stage", "Stage", response_orders$stage),
  summary_rows("discipline_1", "Discipline", summary_disciplines,
               labels = replace(summary_disciplines, 5, "Social Sciences"))
)
rownames(participant_summary) = NULL
write.csv(participant_summary, "participant_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
participant_summary
```

# Nature plots

## Demographics

```{r demographics, results='asis'}
demographic_plots = list()
for (question in demographics) {
  counts = data_filtered |> count(response = .data[[question]])
  p = category_plot(
    counts, question_title(question),

    response_order = response_orders[[question]]
  )
  demographic_plots[[question]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p, name = paste0("demographics-", question))
}
```

## AI questions

```{r ai, results='asis'}
ai_plots = list()
for (question in ai_questions) {
  counts = data_filtered |> count(response = .data[[question]])
  p = category_plot(
    counts, question_title(question),

    response_order = response_orders[[question]]
  )
  ai_plots[[question]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p, name = paste0("ai-", question))
}
```

## AI questions as waffle plots

Each square represents approximately 1% of valid responses. Square counts are
rounded to total exactly 100; legend percentages use the original response counts.

```{r ai-waffles, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
for (question in ai_questions) {
  answers = response_orders[[question]]
  counts = data_filtered |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[question]]), nzchar(trimws(.data[[question]]))) |>
    count(response = factor(.data[[question]], levels = answers), .drop = FALSE) |>
    mutate(percentage = n / sum(n),
           squares = diff(c(0, round(cumsum(percentage) * 100))))

  tiles = counts |>
    tidyr::uncount(squares) |>
    mutate(x = (row_number() - 1) %/% 10 + 1,
           y = 10 - (row_number() - 1) %% 10)

  palette = response_palette(answers)
  labels = legend_response_labels(question, answers, counts$percentage)

  p = ggplot(tiles, aes(x, y, fill = response)) +
    geom_tile(width = 0.9, height = 0.9, key_glyph = draw_key_square) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.65) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(palette, answers), labels = labels, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(title = question_title(question),
         subtitle = participant_subtitle(sum(counts$n)),
         fill = NULL, caption = notes("Each tile is approximately 1%; legend shows actual percentages. Missing answers excluded.")) +
    theme_nature() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(margin = margin(b = 18))) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE))
  print(p)
}
```


## AI roles

Each horizontal bar shows the four autonomy options for one role, from not
permitted to human supervision, autonomous use, and unsure. Percentages exclude
missing responses separately for each role and sum to 100% within each bar.
The All roles bar pools valid answers across all six roles.

```{r ai-roles, fig.width=12, fig.height=8 + title_height(question_title("ai_roles"))}
role_response_order = c("Not permitted", "Permitted with human supervision",
                        "Permitted autonomously", "Unsure")

role_responses = data_filtered |>
  select(all_of(names(ai_roles))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "role", values_to = "response") |>
  mutate(response = trimws(response)) |>
  filter(!is.na(response), nzchar(response))

# Fail visibly if the survey introduces an answer not covered by this ordering.
stopifnot(all(role_responses$response %in% role_response_order))

role_counts = bind_rows(role_responses, role_responses |> mutate(role = ".all_roles")) |>
  mutate(role = factor(role, levels = c(rev(names(ai_roles)), ".all_roles")),
         response = factor(response, levels = role_response_order)) |>
  count(role, response, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(role) |>
  mutate(total = sum(n),
         percentage = if_else(total > 0, n / total, NA_real_)) |>
  ungroup()

# Explicit cumulative positions keep the requested left-to-right stack order.
role_counts = role_counts |>
  arrange(role, response) |>
  group_by(role) |>
  mutate(xmax = cumsum(percentage), xmin = xmax - percentage,
         label = stacked_percent_label(percentage)) |>
  ungroup()
role_palette = setNames(academic_colours$responses[c(1, 4, 5, 3)],
                         role_response_order)
role_rgb = grDevices::col2rgb(role_palette) / 255
role_linear = ifelse(role_rgb <= 0.04045, role_rgb / 12.92,
                     ((role_rgb + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
role_luminance = colSums(role_linear * c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722))
role_text = setNames(ifelse(role_luminance < 0.179, "white", "black"),
                     names(role_palette))
role_counts$text_colour = unname(role_text[as.character(role_counts$response)])
role_labels = c(ai_roles, .all_roles = "All roles")

ai_roles_plot = ggplot(role_counts, aes(y = role, fill = response)) +
  geom_rect(key_glyph = draw_key_square, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,
                ymin = as.numeric(role) - 0.38, ymax = as.numeric(role) + 0.38),
            color = "white", linewidth = 0.4, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, label = label, color = text_colour),
            show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = role_palette, breaks = role_response_order,
                    labels = c("Not permitted", "With human supervision", "Autonomously", "Unsure"),
                    drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE,
                   labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(unname(role_labels[x]), width = 30)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(title = question_title("ai_roles"),
       subtitle = participant_subtitle(nrow(data_filtered |>
         filter(if_any(all_of(names(ai_roles)), ~ !is.na(.x) & nzchar(trimws(.x)))))),

       x = "Share of respondents within each role", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = notes("Percentages exclude missing responses separately for each role. All roles pools valid role answers; each participant can contribute one answer per role. Labels shown for segments with percentages ≥ 5%. Percentages may not total 100 because of rounding.")) +
  theme_nature() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(margin = margin(b = 6)))

ai_roles_plot
```

## AI change

```{r ai-change, results='asis'}
# Multiple selections: denominators count people answering the question, not selections.
change_respondents = data_filtered |>
  select(respondent, stage, change) |>
  filter(!is.na(change), nzchar(trimws(change)))
training_option = "I am considering training fewer researchers."

change_long = change_respondents |>
  select(respondent, change) |>
  separate_longer_delim(change, delim = ",") |>
  mutate(change = trimws(change)) |>
  filter(nzchar(change)) |>
  distinct(respondent, change)
stopifnot(all(change_long$change %in% response_orders$change))

# Exclude PhD students from both numerator and denominator for training only.
change_eligible = tidyr::expand_grid(
  respondent = change_respondents$respondent,
  response = response_orders$change
) |>
  left_join(select(change_respondents, respondent, stage), by = "respondent") |>
  filter(!(response == training_option & coalesce(stage == "PhD student", FALSE))) |>
  left_join(change_long |> transmute(respondent, response = change, chosen = TRUE),
            by = c("respondent", "response"))

change_counts = change_eligible |>
  group_by(response) |>
  summarise(n = sum(chosen %in% TRUE), denominator = n(), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(change_counts$n <= change_counts$denominator))

change_plot = category_plot(
  change_counts, question_title("change"),

  response_order = response_orders$change, participants = nrow(change_respondents)
) + labs(caption = notes(paste(
  "Multiple selections allowed; percentages can sum to more than 100%.",
  "Training fewer researchers excludes PhD students.",
  "Responses with conflicting selections are excluded from this question.",
  sep = "\n"
)))
# Reserve space for the denominator explanation.
attr(change_plot, "figure_height") = attr(change_plot, "figure_height") + 0.5
show_survey_plot(change_plot, name = "ai-change-bars")
```

```{r ai-by-discipline, results='asis'}
# Rank disciplines by strong agreement and keep natural-science fields within their parent segment.
# Awareness uses the most familiar response; capability uses the two highest levels.
discipline_rank_responses = list(
  awareness = "Very familiar",
  capability = response_orders$capability[4:5],
  displacement = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree"),
  threat = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree"),
  opportunity = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree"),
  concern = c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree")
)
for (question in ai_questions) {
  p = grouped_ai_plot(data_filtered, question, "discipline_of_interest",
                      discipline_order, "discipline",
                      rank_responses = discipline_rank_responses[[question]],
                      hierarchy_parent = "Natural sciences")
  grouped_plots[[paste0("discipline_", question)]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p)
}
```

## AI questions by subfield within disciplines

Each set compares the lower-level fields within one primary discipline. The
All respondents bar pools valid answers within that discipline, including
respondents who did not specify a subfield. Other subfield categories are retained.

```{r ai-by-subfield, results='asis'}
subfield_disciplines = c(
  social_sciences = "Social sciences",
  medical_life_sciences = "Medical, health and life sciences",
  engineering = "Engineering and technology"
)

# Shorten only the displayed labels; preserve the survey categories in the data.
subfield_labels = c(
  "Electrical engineering, computer engineering, and information engineering" =
    "Electrical, computer & information engineering",
  "Civil engineering, maritime engineering, transport engineering, and mining engineering" =
    "Civil, maritime, transport & mining eng.",
  "Environmental engineering and related engineering" =
    "Environmental & related engineering",
  "Materials engineering and resources engineering" =
    "Materials & resources engineering",
  "Industrial, systems and processes engineering" =
    "Industrial, systems & process engineering"
)

for (discipline in names(subfield_disciplines)) {
  parent = subfield_disciplines[[discipline]]
  cat("\n\n### ", parent, "\n\n", sep = "")
  discipline_data = data_filtered |> filter(discipline_1 == parent)
  subfield_order = discipline_data$discipline_2
  subfield_order = sort(unique(subfield_order[!is.na(subfield_order) & nzchar(trimws(subfield_order))]))

  for (question in ai_questions) {
    p = grouped_ai_plot(discipline_data, question, "discipline_2", subfield_order,
                        "subfield", rank_responses = discipline_rank_responses[[question]])
    if (is.null(p)) next
    p = p + labs(
      x = "Share of respondents within each subfield",
      caption = sub("All respondents are shown separately and pools valid answers from the full filtered sample.",
                    paste0("The overall bar pools all valid answers within ", parent, "."),
                    p$labels$caption, fixed = TRUE)
    )
    row_labels = p$data |> distinct(group, y) |> arrange(y) |> pull(group)
    y_scale = p$scales$get_scales("y")
    y_scale$labels = stringr::str_wrap(recode(row_labels, !!!subfield_labels), width = 31)
    name = paste("grouped", discipline, "subfields", question, sep = "_")
    attr(p, "figure_label") = name
    grouped_plots[[name]] = p
    show_survey_plot(p)
  }
}
```

## AI question pairs as heatmaps

All unique pairs of the six AI questions are shown once (15 panels).
Each cell is the percentage of respondents selecting that combination, among
those who answered both questions in that panel. The colour scale is shared
across panels; percentages within each panel sum to 100% before rounding.
Axes follow the response orders above, using abbreviated labels for readability.
AI roles remain separate from these questions.

```{r ai-pair-heatmaps, fig.width=24, fig.height=40, dpi=300, fig.retina=1}
# Short axis labels map to the exact survey answers in response_orders.
heatmap_response_labels = list(
  awareness = c("Not aware", "Heard about it;\nknow little",
                "Somewhat\nfamiliar", "Very familiar"),
  capability = c("Cannot help", "Assist humans", "Work independently:\nachieving lower\nquality",
                 "Work independently:\nachieving comparable\nquality", "Work independently:\nachieving higher\nquality")
)
for (question in c("displacement", "threat", "opportunity", "concern")) {
  heatmap_response_labels[[question]] = c(
    "Strongly\ndisagree", "Somewhat\ndisagree", "Neither agree\nnor disagree",
    "Somewhat\nagree", "Strongly\nagree"
  )
}
heatmap_label_lookup = unlist(lapply(ai_questions, function(question) {
  stopifnot(length(heatmap_response_labels[[question]]) == length(response_orders[[question]]))
  setNames(heatmap_response_labels[[question]],
           paste(question, seq_along(response_orders[[question]]), sep = "::"))
}))

ai_question_pairs = combn(ai_questions, 2, simplify = FALSE)
pair_heatmap_data = purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(ai_question_pairs), function(i) {
  pair = ai_question_pairs[[i]]
  row_question = pair[1]
  column_question = pair[2]
  row_answers = response_orders[[row_question]]
  column_answers = response_orders[[column_question]]
  paired = data_filtered |>
    transmute(row_answer = .data[[row_question]],
              column_answer = .data[[column_question]]) |>
    filter(!is.na(row_answer), nzchar(trimws(row_answer)),
           !is.na(column_answer), nzchar(trimws(column_answer)))
  stopifnot(all(paired$row_answer %in% row_answers),
            all(paired$column_answer %in% column_answers))
  paired |>
    count(row_answer, column_answer, name = "count") |>
    complete(row_answer = row_answers, column_answer = column_answers,
             fill = list(count = 0)) |>
    mutate(pair_id = i,
           panel = paste0(question_title(row_question), " (rows) / ",
                          question_title(column_question), " (columns)"),
           row_key = paste(row_question, match(row_answer, row_answers), sep = "::"),
           column_key = paste(column_question, match(column_answer, column_answers), sep = "::"),
           total = nrow(paired),
           proportion = if (nrow(paired) > 0) count / nrow(paired) else NA_real_)
})

# Unique keys allow each facet to retain its own semantic response order.
heatmap_keys = unlist(lapply(ai_questions, function(question) {
  paste(question, seq_along(response_orders[[question]]), sep = "::")
}))
pair_heatmap_data = pair_heatmap_data |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)),
         row_key = factor(row_key, levels = rev(heatmap_keys)),
         column_key = factor(column_key, levels = heatmap_keys),
         cell_label = case_when(
           is.na(proportion) ~ "-",
           count == 0 ~ "0",
           proportion < 0.01 ~ "<1",
           TRUE ~ sprintf("%.0f", 100 * proportion)
         ))

pair_checks = pair_heatmap_data |>
  group_by(pair_id) |>
  summarise(total = first(total), cells = sum(count), share = sum(proportion), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(pair_checks) == choose(length(ai_questions), 2),
          all(pair_checks$cells == pair_checks$total),
          all(abs(pair_checks$share[pair_checks$total > 0] - 1) < 1e-10))

heatmap_max = max(c(0.01, pair_heatmap_data$proportion), na.rm = TRUE)
# Match label contrast to the actual fill, including both dark palette ends.
heatmap_fills = scales::col_numeric(rev(tokyo_colours), domain = c(0, heatmap_max),
                                   na.color = academic_colours$missing)(pair_heatmap_data$proportion)
heatmap_rgb = grDevices::col2rgb(heatmap_fills) / 255
heatmap_linear = ifelse(heatmap_rgb <= 0.04045, heatmap_rgb / 12.92,
                        ((heatmap_rgb + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
heatmap_luminance = colSums(heatmap_linear * c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722))
pair_heatmap_data$text_colour = ifelse(heatmap_luminance < 0.179, "white", "black")
ai_pairs_plot = ggplot(pair_heatmap_data,
                       aes(x = column_key, y = row_key, fill = proportion)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = cell_label, color = text_colour),
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = rev(tokyo_colours),
                      limits = c(0, heatmap_max), na.value = academic_colours$missing,
                      labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                      name = "Share of paired responses") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) unname(heatmap_label_lookup[x]),
                   expand = expansion(add = 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) unname(heatmap_label_lookup[x]),
                   expand = expansion(add = 0)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), ncol = 3, scales = "free",
             labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 42)) +
  labs(title = "AI questions: all pairwise response distributions",
       subtitle = participant_subtitle(sum(rowSums(sapply(data_filtered[ai_questions],
         function(x) !is.na(x) & nzchar(trimws(x)))) >= 2)),
       x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = notes("One panel per unique pair; shared colour scale. Missing answers excluded separately for each pair.\n0 = no responses; <1 = less than 1%; - = no paired responses. Percentages may not sum to 100 after rounding.")) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(lineheight = 1.05,
                                    margin = margin(t = 8)),
        axis.text.y = element_text(lineheight = 1.05,
                                    margin = margin(r = 8)),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(24, "pt"),
        panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(30, "pt"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = plot_label_size, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 12)),
        plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(margin = margin(b = 20))) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = grid::unit(220, "pt"),
                               barheight = grid::unit(12, "pt"), title.position = "top"))

ai_pairs_plot
```
